title: TIME: ICE Detention Fatality Rate Reaches 22-Year High as Agency Cuts Death Reporting
excerpt: A TIME investigation published August 10, 2026, found that the fatality rate in ICE custody had reached a 22-year high in the opening months of fiscal year 2026, according to research published in JAMA. The report also documented that ICE was simultaneously reducing its public death-reporting obligations.
content:
TIME magazine's August 10, 2026, investigation drew on JAMA research and government records to document the unprecedented death toll in ICE detention during the current fiscal year.

  • The JAMA study found the annual mortality rate in ICE custody hit 88.9 per 100,000 person-years in the partial fiscal year 2026 — the highest rate in the 22-year study period, exceeding even the COVID-19 era spike.
  • The number of people in ICE detention rose roughly 70 percent — from approximately 40,000 before Trump's return to office to over 68,000 in February 2026.
  • Amid the rising fatality rate, ICE reduced the information it makes public about detainee deaths, and the agency announced it would stop reporting instances when people die soon after being released from custody.

JAMA editorial authors wrote that the spike took place in a system with "longstanding failures" compounded by Trump administration policies that "rapidly expanded detention to historically high levels, weakened oversight mechanisms, and worsened conditions of confinement."
